what: Comparing Two Groups (Binary Variable) for a Binary Variable
title: Overview and Introduction to VISCfunctions Package
text: two_samp_bin_test() used comparing binary variable binary (two group) variable, options Barnard, Fisher’s Exact, Chi-Sq, McNemar tests. Barnard test specifically, many model options can set get passed Exact::exact.test() function.
code: table(testing_data$response, testing_data$group) #>     #>     1 2 #>   0 2 0 #>   1 4 6  # Barnard Method two_samp_bin_test(   x = testing_data$response,   y = testing_data$group,   method = 'barnard',   alternative = 'two.sided' ) #> [1] 0.1970196  # Santner and Snell Variation two_samp_bin_test(   x = testing_data$response,   y = testing_data$group,   method = 'barnard',   barnard_method = 'santner and snell',   alternative = 'two.sided') #> [1] 0.3876953  # Calling test multiple times exampleData_BAMA |>    group_by(antigen, visitno) |>    filter(visitno != 0) |>    summarise(p_val = two_samp_bin_test(response, group, method = 'barnard'), .groups = "drop") #> # A tibble: 14 × 3 #>    antigen               visitno p_val #>    <chr>                   <dbl> <dbl> #>  1 A1.con.env03 140 CF         1 0.197 #>  2 A1.con.env03 140 CF         2 1     #>  3 A244 D11gp120 avi           1 1     #>  4 A244 D11gp120 avi           2 1     #>  5 B.63521 D11gp120/293F       1 0.518 #>  6 B.63521 D11gp120/293F       2 1     #>  7 B.MN V3 gp70                1 0.197 #>  8 B.MN V3 gp70                2 1     #>  9 B.con.env03 140 CF          1 1     #> 10 B.con.env03 140 CF          2 1     #> 11 gp41                        1 0.667 #> 12 gp41                        2 0.774 #> 13 p24                         1 1     #> 14 p24                         2 0.197

title: Create a data.frame to plot MB curves and AUC — mb_results

title: Create a data.frame to plot MB curves and AUC — mb_results
code: mb_results(   magnitude,   response = NULL,   lower_trunc = 100,   upper_trunc = 22000,   x_transform = c("log10", "raw") )

title: Create a data.frame to plot MB curves and AUC — mb_results
text: magnitude values create step curve AUC (numeric vector) response response status, vector type integer (0/1) logical (TRUE/FALSE). NULL assumes response information considered. lower_trunc lower truncation value (numeric scalar must 0 higher). upper_trunc upper truncation value (numeric scalar must higher lower_trunc). Set Inf upper truncation x_transform character vector specifying transformation AUC calculation, . Must one "log10" (default) "raw".

title: Create a data.frame to plot MB curves and AUC — mb_results
text: Returns data frame following columns: * magnitude - magnitude values (similar times survival analysis) * breadth - percent antigens greater equal magnitude value * n_remaining - number antigens remaining greater equal magnitude value * n_here - number antigens exact magnitude value * aucMB - area magnitude breadth curve

title: Create a data.frame to plot MB curves and AUC — mb_results
text: AUC calculated 0 (1 x_transform = "log10") x values (lower_trunc/upper_trunc x value truncation). response given, non-responding values (response = 0 FALSE) values set lower_trunc MB curves AUC calculations. output can used plotting step function curves, magnitude x axis breadth y axis. Note x_transform = 'log10' resulting plot best displayed log10 scale (ggplot2::scale_x_log10). aucMB can used boxplots group comparisons. Note aucMB repeated values magnitude breadth.

title: Create a data.frame to plot MB curves and AUC — mb_results

title: Pairwise Testing for a Continuous Variable — pairwise_test_cont
text: Returns data frame possible pairwise comparisons: Comparison - Comparisons made SampleSizes - number samples per group Median_Min_Max - Median [Min, Max] per group Mean_SD - Mean(sd) per group (log10_stats = FALSE) Mean - Geometric mean per group (log10_stats = TRUE) log_Mean_SD - Mean(sd) per group log10 x scale (log10_stats = TRUE) MagnitudeTest - wilcox/t-test test p value PerfectSeparation - logical flag indicating perfect separation Returns data frame possible pairwise comparisons.
